# `sensor_flow_across_frequencies`

whether the sensor flow moves at the same speed and direction across frequencies - the cosines of the atoms' flows, direction consistency and the slope of speed against frequency.

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run sensor_flow_across_frequencies --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run sensor_flow_across_frequencies --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run sensor_flow_across_frequencies --dataset D --subject S --flow NAME --package hodgeDirac__SURFACE --atoms ATOMS
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `recording` | field recording, each true, where {"name": "$recording"}, read shape (the recording the sensor flow read (its measurements are of it)) | yes |
| `edges` | measurement phase_current, of recording, where {"name": "$atoms"} (the sensor flow's phase current per edge and atom (`nxr-neuro run sensor_flow` first)) | yes |
| `modes` | measurement flow_coefficient, of recording, where {"name": "$atoms"} (the sensor flow's Hodge-Dirac coefficients per atom) | yes |
| `power` | measurement power, of recording, where {"name": "$atoms"} (the sensor flow's power per vertex and atom) | yes |
| `current_x` | measurement vertex_phase_current_x, of recording, where {"name": "$atoms"} | yes |
| `current_y` | measurement vertex_phase_current_y, of recording, where {"name": "$atoms"} | yes |
| `current_z` | measurement vertex_phase_current_z, of recording, where {"name": "$atoms"} | yes |
| `package` | operator eigenvectors, where {"name": "${package}_eigenvectors"} (the sensor surface's Hodge-Dirac solve the flow is on) | yes |
| `atoms` | selection any, where {"name": "$atoms"} (the frequency atoms the flow was read with) | yes |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `recording` | `--recording` | `none` | - |  | the recording the sensor flow read, or none: every recording of the subject, one run each |
| `package` | `--package` | none | - |  | the Hodge-Dirac solve's stem |
| `atoms` | `--atoms` | none | - |  | the frequency atoms' kernel set by name |
| `name` | `--name` | `{recording}_{package}_across_frequencies` | - |  | the stem of the stored statistics: <name>_atom_pairs, <name>_dispersion |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`signal.flow_across_frequencies`](../nodes.md) | edges=edges, modes=modes, power=power, current_x=current_x, current_y=current_y, current_z=current_z, package=package, frequency=atoms |  | atom_pairs, dispersion |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `atom_pairs` | kind statistic, name {name}_atom_pairs, of recording |
| `dispersion` | kind statistic, name {name}_dispersion, of recording |

## Notes from the definition

```text
DOES THE FLOW MOVE AT THE SAME SPEED AND IN THE SAME DIRECTION ACROSS FREQUENCIES? (spec docs/specs/2026-11-24-bispectrum.md, "The flow across frequencies"): a readout of the sensor
flow pipeline's own per-atom results, a statistic over the members of the atoms' level. It reads stored results, never the recording.

THE GRAPH. before: the flow's stored per-atom sums (sensor_flow's <name>_flow_edges, <name>_flow_modes, <name>_flow_vertices: signal.spectral_flow's whole field) + the Hodge-Dirac
package + the atoms they were read with --[signal.flow_across_frequencies]--> per pair of atoms the cosines of their flows (edges in the Hodge inner product, travel coefficients,
rotation coefficients); per vertex the direction consistency across atoms (resultant length of the unit vertex phase currents) and the slope of log apparent speed against log
frequency (0: the same speed; 1: the same wavelength).
An event's flow is compared by the same node from the atoms' time cells within the event (graph in the spec; not wired here).

What it cannot resolve: the apparent speed is an upper bound; a whole-run flow keeps the net quadrature only; one run gives descriptions, not a test (events or runs are the replicates).

  nxr-neuro run sensor_flow_across_frequencies --dataset D --subject S --flow NAME --package hodgeDirac__SURFACE --atoms ATOMS
```
